clue.text: Conceited youngster, a future skipper, possibly

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky, conceited young man, as in 'an insolent young pup'

explanation.surface: A cocky lad is tipped to captain the side one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' suggests a team or ship's captain, but it is a butterfly, the skipper family; 'possibly' warns that this is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrysalis is the resting stage before an insect emerges as an adult, so it may become a skipper butterfly.

clue.text: The type who bothers with duck sauce

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance who bothers people
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Someone annoying fusses over the duck with sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genoese basil, pine-nut and parmesan paste is a classic pasta sauce.

clue.text: Eliminate European side at Lord's

parts.note: Polish means from Poland, a European country
in cricket, the off side is one half of the field; Lord's is London's famous cricket ground

explanation.surface: A European team is knocked out at the home of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the London home of cricket; the OFF side is the half of the field the batter faces.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish off or dispose of something completely is to get rid of it.

clue.text: Water very quietly absorbed in part of body

indicators.note: one thing absorbed in another is taken inside it, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: Adam's ale is an old jocular name for plain water, the only drink Adam had
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone takes a sip of water without a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' looks like the definition, but ADAM'S ALE is an old joke name for it, since Adam had nothing else to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulge of cartilage at the front of a man's throat carries this name.

clue.text: Liberal university in commitment that distributes power

indicators.note: the pieces before it go in the next word, inside it

parts.note: devotion is dedicated commitment

explanation.surface: A Liberal college is committed to sharing out authority.
explanation.walkthrough: LU goes inside DEVOTION, between its V and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the handing down of central government authority to regions, so the clue's 'that distributes power' describes the process.

clue.text: Times supporting a chap such as Douglas?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: a man is a chap
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper backs a fellow called Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper; it is the sign X. Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Things from the Isle of Man take this adjective, and Douglas is the island's capital.

clue.text: Drinks provided in wild parties

indicators.note: the first piece goes in the second, sitting inside it
wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: if means provided that

explanation.surface: Drinks are laid on at riotous gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' reads as 'supplied', but it is the conditional IF; 'wild' rearranges PARTIES to APERTS around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholic drinks taken before a meal to sharpen the appetite.

clue.text: Fraudulent type raised charges by minimal amount

parts.note: p, a penny, is the smallest amount of British money

indicators.note: in a down clue, something raised is turned upward, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: dues are charges or fees

explanation.surface: A con artist hiked his fees by a whisker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns DUES into SEUD; P (a penny) goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretentious poser who pretends to knowledge or culture is a sham.

clue.text: Seen tu run off between you and me

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words as printed, with the slip 'tu' standing for 'to', so the fodder is the letters of seen to run

explanation.surface: Someone was spotted running away, confidentially speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'tu', a slip for 'to'; 'off' rearranges SEEN TO RUN into the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means privately, in confidence, literally 'among us'.

clue.text: Facts making American a little upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: a tad is a little

explanation.surface: Some information leaves an American slightly unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses A + TAD (ATAD).
explanation.definitionFit: Information or figures gathered for analysis are facts.

clue.text: Promotion of number one

parts.note: number one is a jokey way of saying oneself, so promoting number one means pushing one's own career forward

explanation.surface: A firm's top person gets a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like the boss or a chart-topper, but it means oneself, as in 'looking after number one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Furthering one's own interests or position is exactly what promoting yourself amounts to.

clue.text: A barrier to progress for some races

definitions.text: A barrier to progress for some races

parts.words: A barrier to progress for some races
parts.note: reads like a social comment on peoples held back, but really describes a hurdle or fence on a course in steeplechases and similar events

explanation.surface: A remark about what holds certain peoples back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Races' suggests ethnic groups; it means contests such as steeplechases.
explanation.definitionFit: Any hindrance is a barrier, and the fences in a steeplechase or assault course give such races their name.

clue.text: One watched for a shot that delights a golfer

definitions.meaning: photographers once told sitters to 'watch the ...' so they looked at the camera for the photograph
a score of one under par on a hole, which pleases any golfer

explanation.surface: Something at which a golfer aims a pleasing stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' seems to be golf throughout, but the first half is a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fixed uses: the imaginary bird at the camera lens and the golf score one below par.

clue.text: Disc that's likely to be hit soon after launch

definitions.text: Disc that's likely to be hit soon after launch

parts.words: Disc that's likely to be hit soon after launch
parts.note: describes a target flung into the air and shot by marksmen, while seeming to describe a record or a rocket

explanation.surface: A new record is tipped to become a hit right after its release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disc', 'hit' and 'launch' suggest pop music; it is trap shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: The clay saucer thrown from a trap and shot at in the sport of skeet.

clue.text: Wade across one? Hardly!

indicators.note: one word stretched across another sits around it, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: to ford a river is to wade across it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that a stretch of water could be waded through.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a deep sea inlet is the last place you could ford, hence 'Hardly!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norwegian-style sea inlet between steep cliffs is far too deep for anyone to cross on foot.

clue.text: The airs that people put on!

definitions.text: The airs that people put on!

parts.words: The airs that people put on!
parts.note: reads as pretentious behaviour, but means tunes, airs, that ordinary people perform

explanation.surface: An exclamation at people's pretensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airs' seems to mean affectations; it means songs, and 'put on' means perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional songs passed down among ordinary people form this genre.

clue.text: Ancient intriguing led to her death

definitions.text: Ancient intriguing led to her death

parts.words: Ancient intriguing led to her death
parts.note: in Othello, Iago is called 'the ancient' (an old word for ensign), and his plotting got Othello's wife killed

explanation.surface: Some old scheming proved fatal to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' is a rank, ensign, held by Iago in Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's wife, smothered after Iago's scheming makes her husband jealous.

clue.text: Reprimand from oriental king tolerated

indicators.note: the answer comes out from within the following run of words, spanning their join

explanation.surface: An Eastern monarch puts up with being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'orienTAL KING TOlerated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down or scolding is a noun for the same telling-off.

clue.text: Model of chivalry pronounced the latest word?

indicators.note: pronounced means the words are said aloud and spelt as something else that sounds the same

parts.note: a good knight is a model of chivalry

explanation.surface: An ideal of knighthood made the final pronouncement.
explanation.walkthrough: The word said at bedtime is the last word of the day, hence 'latest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell said at the end of the day, last thing before sleep.

clue.text: One person's tale is inaccurate about female politician

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes round it, so the next letter is enclosed

parts.note: someone who lies is being inaccurate
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A woman MP's biography is said to be full of errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inaccurate' looks like the anagram signal, but 'is inaccurate' means LIES. TORY is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A biography is the account of a single individual's experiences from birth onward.

clue.text: No longer taxes people up North

definitions.meaning: scot was an old tax or levy, as in 'scot-free', so the plural is an archaic word for taxes
natives of Scotland, which lies in the north of Britain

explanation.surface: Northerners are relieved of their taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot-free' originally meant free of the scot, a medieval tax.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an obsolete levy, the other the nationality of Scotland's inhabitants.

clue.text: Mouse taken to guy

definitions.meaning: to take the ... is to mock, and to guy someone is to ridicule them

explanation.surface: A mouse is carried to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the verb meaning to make fun of: when this word is taken, someone is guyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon rodent is the first sense; the second completes the idiom 'take the ...', meaning tease.

clue.text: Hot and sick after getting cold like this

definitions.text: Hot and sick after getting cold like this

indicators.note: the pieces before these words come after the one that follows them

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone feels feverish and poorly after catching cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: catching cold leaves you hot and sick with one.
explanation.definitionFit: A feverish cold with shivering is an illness caught from being cold.

clue.text: Fellow's agitation describing dons

parts.note: his is the possessive for a male fellow
panic is a state of agitation

explanation.surface: University fellows are thrown into alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' suggests Oxbridge academics, but here they are Spanish gentlemen, addressed as Don.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for Spanish-speaking people, and 'Don' is the Spanish honorific for a gentleman.

clue.text: Sort of memory that follows piano concert

indicators.note: one piece that follows another comes after it in the answer

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
ROM is read-only memory in computing

explanation.surface: A recollection that comes after a piano recital.
explanation.walkthrough: PROMS are the BBC's summer promenade concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade concert, where some of the audience stands, as at London's Proms.

clue.text: Penny each, possibly

parts.note: a price of only a penny apiece would be a bargain

explanation.surface: A price tag of a penny apiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-priced, inexpensive, as anything costing a penny would be.

clue.text: Objections raised in short piece

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means turned upward, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Objections are raised to a brief article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like the objections being voiced; it reverses BUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stump or remaining fragment, like a ticket counterfoil or cigarette end.

clue.text: It's said to be a careless error

definitions.text: It's said to be a careless error

parts.words: It's said to be a careless error
parts.note: a mistake made in speaking rather than writing, so it is indeed something said

explanation.surface: A remark that something is reckoned to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' reads like hearsay but literally means the error is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal blunder is an inadvertent mistake made while talking.

clue.text: Book individual after arrest, finding part of skeleton

indicators.note: after means the pieces before it in the clue come later in the answer

parts.note: to collar someone is slang for arresting them
one is an individual, a single person

explanation.surface: A suspect is booked once the police have nabbed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like the police charging someone, but it is just B.
explanation.definitionFit: The clavicle, the bone joining shoulder blade to breastbone, is part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Characters in front of queue, say, in dominant position

definitions.text: Characters in front of queue, say
definitions.meaning: queue sounds like the letter Q, and the letters ahead of it in the alphabet run from A to P
on top of, above everything else

explanation.surface: People at the head of a line are top dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are letters, not people, and 'queue, say' is the letter Q.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top of something puts you above everything else, in a commanding place.
